text:
elaine: Heads up — quick design question on cost accounting when we fan out a single request to multiple model variants for latency fallbacks. Do we double-charge, prorate, or pick one canonical attribution?
ryan: we currently emit one raw event per infer call to each backend variant. billing side just sums tokens, so yeah double-charge if we don't dedupe.
jen: That's intentional in some cases (customers asked to pay for all compute used). But it causes surprising spikes in invoice preview when fallbacks kick in.
sam: Could we tag events with `request_fanout_id` and a `charge_type` flag? e.g. `charge_type: primary|probe|shadow` and then invoice pipeline can decide policy.
alex: +1, but we need to be careful about backfill/replay windows. If pipeline dedupes by fanout id, any late-arriving probe after the primary could be dropped and cause token undercount for real usage.
elaine: Good point. Current ingest TTL is 48h for dedupe. Would that be enough?
jen: For most customers yes, but enterprise billing enforcements want finality at 30 days for disputes. We can keep canonical ledger that prefers `primary` records and only uses probes for observability.
billing-bot: auto-note: policy PRD required if we change invoice outcomes. See #finance for approval.
ryan: Operationally we could do two things: 1) keep raw events in analytics stream, 2) emit a "billing-ready" stream where we run attribution rules (dedupe, pick primary, prorate). The latter is what invoices read.
maria: Is there a case where prorating across variants makes sense? e.g., customer uses a safe-fallback path where we run a small cheap model then run a larger model only if needed — do we charge both?
jen: I'd argue charge for the one that produced the final output that the customer consumed. But for streaming/partial responses this is messy.
sam: Example payload idea: ```json
{
  "req_id": "req_abc123",
  "fanout_id": "fan_zzz",
  "variant": "gpt-lite-quant",
  "role": "probe",
  "tokens": 24
}
```
elaine: If we go this route, the billing-ready transform would: prefer role==primary, else if only probes exist, sum probes? Or optionally prorate by model compute cost factor.
ryan: cost factor table is already in the catalog service. We could attach `compute_units` to each billing-ready record and then invoices multiply by unit price. That handles heterogenous model costs.
alex: Implementation note: make sure the `billing-ready` stream has an idempotent dedupe key: `tenant|date|fanout_id|variant` — and perhaps a finalizer that emits a single `final_charge` event once per `fanout_id` when we decide canonical attribution.
maria: UX question: how do we surface this to customers in the console preview? They expect invoice preview to be stable during canary rollouts.
jen: We should add an explanation tooltip: "Requests that try multiple models may show probe compute in analytics but will be billed according to your chosen fallback policy: primary-only | prorate | charge-all." Make primary-only the default for now.
elaine: Action items: (1) eng-platform to sketch transform spec for billing-ready stream and finalizer, (2) billing and finance to sign off on default policy, (3) product to draft console UX copy and invoice-preview toggles.
ryan: I'll draft the transform pseudo-logic: ```sql
-- pseudocode for billing-ready
select tenant, fanout_id, coalesce(primary.variant, cheapest.variant) as billed_variant, sum(tokens*compute_units) as total_compute_units
from raw_events
group by tenant, fanout_id
```
sam: Danger: SQL-style group means late arrivals might move results. Need watermarking or a "finalize" window. Let's aim for a 1h soft window and 7d finalize for disputes.
elaine: ok. I'll open a short ADR describing tradeoffs and propose: soft-window=1h (for near-real-time preview), finalize=7d (for invoice locking), dispute window=30d.
jen: sounds reasonable. Finance: please confirm.
billing-bot: auto-note: created ticket FIN-458: "Confirm fanout billing default policy"
ryan: tagging @maria so product can think about console toggle placement.
maria: on it — I'll mock a preview modal showing "Billing policy for multi-variant requests" and include the tooltip copy.
elaine: thanks all. ping if you want to pair on the transform spec. :white_check_mark:
